extra.description: free-text note from the shot's author: derivations, caveats, and which existing repo function this shot's check must call

max_mm_per_px.description: resolution ceiling: a smaller number is a finer image

span_axis.description: which silhouette dimension min_subject_px is measured along. Absent, or 'path' for a distance along the cloth, means the check bounds the requirement rather than asserting it -- no path inside a subject exceeds its bounding box.

camera_position.description: where the operator and camera stand

instance_of.description: feature key this shot is templated over; one shot is emitted per counted instance

must_be_empty.description: this frame must show an EMPTY surface. 'A person confirmed it' is the weakest possible evidence for the one frame whose whole content is an absence, and an absence is the easiest thing in this system to measure.

relay_after.description: the shot_id this frame must be an independent RE-LAY of. relay_between_reps chains repeats within one shot id; a repeatability series written as separate shot ids (F00.R1..R5) needs this, or the relay check has nothing to compare against and the series is five photographs of one lay.

rep_semantics.description: What each repeat of this shot is OF, one entry per repeat, where the repeats are different physical subjects rather than repetitions of one view. min_reps alone said 'take two', and nothing recorded that repeat 2 was the other leg -- so two photographs of the same leg satisfied both, and the right leg's original hem was never photographed at all.

requires_human.description: claims a person must confirm for this frame, named by the check id. For frames whose content no automatic check can judge -- an empty backdrop, a lighting test, a coplanarity proof -- this is the only thing standing between the requirement and a photograph of anything.

shot_id.description: stable dotted id; never reused for a different frame

description: The versioned, machine-readable capture list. It is the ONLY source of what a state requires: the readiness gate enumerates required shots from this document, so a shot that is not here is not required, and a shot that is here cannot be skipped by application code.

unanswered_means.description: What the plan assumes before the operator answers. 'present' is the safe default for anything that gates a shot: an unanswered question must never silently drop a capture. 'absent' is permitted only where assuming presence would demand an impossible shot. 'blocks' means the plan cannot be generated at all until answered.

postwash_coverage_decisions.description: One entry for every region that is photographed before the wash, changes with washing, and has no frame in any later state. Each says why. `offcut` means the region leaves with the offcut at a shorts-length cut and its post-wash evidence is in the offcut states. `open` means nobody has decided, and is recorded as undecided rather than assumed sufficient -- the wash is a one-way door, so the frame that is missing is one nobody can ever take.

gate.description: id of the gate that must pass before leaving this state

irreversible_after.description: true when the physical act that follows this state cannot be undone, so the gate must hold before it

title: Pilot capture shot-plan specification
